Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad and the node treats the final spatial relation as sufficient proof of fulfillment. In the edited image, a mug is indeed to the right of the headphones, but the source shows the mug on their left; the edit also leaves a mug-like object on the left and appears to introduce another mug on the right. Thus the requested move has progressed, but the image does not clearly establish that the original mug was moved, which is consistent with partial rather than complete fulfillment. Make the node compare the same target across source and edited snapshots, using stable visual identity/appearance and position, and distinguish a completed move from a newly added duplicate or an unresolved identity. Preserve the rubric’s partial and unknown outcomes: do not infer no progress from ambiguity, or completion from the right-side relation alone. The two support observations are highly confident but appear to repeat the same endpoint claim, not independently verify object continuity; treat that as an evidence/criterion gap, not a transport or dependency failure (all checks ran successfully).
s2: The binding checks only whether some mug is right of the headphones, so it can pass on a newly introduced mug while the original target remains unresolved. Compare the source mug with candidate mugs in the edited snapshot using stable visible attributes (not position alone), and assess whether that same mug moved relative to the headphones. The source shows a distinctive blue mug left of the headphones; the edit appears to retain a mug-like object on the left and shows a different-looking mug on the right, so the endpoint relation alone does not establish completion. Keep partial when there is evidence of progress but continuity/completion is unclear, and unknown when the required identity or movement evidence cannot be resolved; do not turn ambiguity into either no progress or a confident pass. The dependency and execution traces succeeded, so address the criterion/evidence gap rather than transport or schema.
s1: The node’s role is evidence availability, not fulfillment, so keep its criterion narrowly focused on whether the mug and headphones can be identified and their positions judged; do not make a right-of relation or successful movement a pass condition. Its current binding is truncated/ambiguous (“(...)”) and the trace overclaims certainty by treating any visible mug as the target. Clarify the typed binding to compare the source target with edited candidates using stable appearance as well as position, and report identity/continuity as unresolved when the edited image cannot establish which mug is the original. Here the source has a distinctive blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blue blur on the left and two pale mugs, with headphones between them. This supports progress but does not establish that the original mug was moved or that the requested final state is complete. Preserve partial and unknown distinctions rather than converting ambiguity into a confident pass or no progress. The check executed successfully with no dependency failures, so this is a criterion/evidence and confidence-calibration issue, not transport or schema.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout is not given the source or edited images, yet its criteria require it to decide whether the original mug remains or whether the right-side mug is additional. The relocation support can report that evidence, but the fulfillment criteria do not faithfully compose its possible outcomes: they allow partial when the original mug remains or the right-side mug is additional, even though the relocation check can fail because the source mug is elsewhere and not to the right, which does not establish progress toward the requested placement. They also do not clearly map a failed relocation check with no progress to absent. Thus the readout can misclassify or leave required cases unresolved.
